summary: Morris County tower built by the state in 1937 with its top section moved from a 1920s Edison tower; now 92 feet and in active service per NHLR.

facts.design: 1937 tower; top 47-foot section and 7x7 foot metal cab moved from a 1920s Edison fire tower, on an extended Aermotor base, 92 feet total

events.note: Built by NJ Forest Fire Service; top section from 1920s Edison tower; Aermotor base extension brought height to 92 feet (NHLR)

evidence.supports: built by NJ Forest Fire Service in 1937
evidence.quote: Greystone Station fire tower was built by the NJ Forest Fire Service in 1937.

evidence.supports: top 47-foot section and cab moved from Edison tower; Aermotor base; 92 feet
evidence.quote: The top 47’ and 7’x7’ metal cab was moved from the Edison fire tower (1920s), with an extended base provided by the Aermotor Co. increasing the height of the rebuilt tower to 92’

evidence.supports: tallest fire tower in northern New Jersey; in active service
evidence.quote: It is the tallest fire tower in northern New Jersey and is in active service.

evidence.supports: 909 feet elevation; 92 feet (28 m) height; Union Hill, Denville
evidence.quote: Greystone Station 909 feet (277 m) 92 feet (28 m) Div. A Sec. A7 A8,(A5, B10) Union Hill, Denville
Union Hill, Denville N40°51.341' W074°30.690' Morris

notes_for_editor: Only two sources (NHLR and Wikipedia), and they agree. A firelookout.org listing (Active, 1937) seen in a search snippet could not be fetched (404) and is not cited. The brief's other name 'WDHA-FM (Dover)' is unverified and not used. Search results included the Greystone Park fire department, a different organization; excluded. No staffing, access or notable fire data found. The Edison tower's location and dismantling date are not in the sources.
